stated.value: one powder formulation; now a different API and excipient blend is being introduced
at the tablet press feed frame
existing NIR pilot follows API concentration in-line
would like to reuse the calibration
a first technical assessment and experiment; a colleague suggests adding Raman so that the old calibration will remain valid

missing: API concentration range and target accuracy for the new formulation
independent laboratory reference method for API content
identity of the new API and excipients (fluorescence risk for Raman)
existing NIR probe, spectrometer range, fiber type and length
feed-frame conditions: powder speed, sampling rate, cleaning, hazardous area
acceptance (go/no-go) criteria for the new model

status_reason: Material, measured quantity (API concentration) and location (tablet press feed frame) are known, so a provisional assessment is possible, but the old calibration cannot be approved for the new blend because NIR models are built and validated for a specific matrix.
answer: The existing NIR calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend: NIR quantification relies on chemometric models built and validated for a specific matrix, so it must be re-tested on the new blend and most likely replaced. Adding Raman does not preserve the old model; a fused NIR+Raman model is a new model that needs its own calibration and validation, although a published feed-frame study reports fused NIR+Raman PLS predicting API potency better than single methods. The first experiment should build a new NIR calibration for the new blend and compare it with Raman (785 nm) and a fused NIR+Raman model on the same independent reference data.

inline.headline: Test NIR + Raman in the tablet press feed frame with a new calibration for the new blend, against NIR alone.
inline.probe: NIR diffuse reflection probe plus a 785 nm Raman contact probe, or a combined NIRaman probe that fits the feed frame
inline.install: feed frame of the rotary tablet press, where the existing NIR pilot already measures
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica (350–2400 nm) for NIR; silica, preferably Al/Cu-coated to avoid jacket fluorescence, for Raman
inline.test_against: NIR diffuse reflection alone with a new calibration for the new blend
inline.not_final_because: The old calibration must be re-tested and replaced, the fusion gain is from one published study and is only a hypothesis for this blend, Raman may be masked by fluorescence of the new API or excipients, and the concentration range, reference method and acceptance criteria are not yet known.

problems.text: The existing calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new formulation: NIR calibrations are chemometric models built and validated for a specific matrix, and a different API and excipient blend is a new matrix, so the old model must be re-tested and most likely replaced by a new calibration.

Adding Raman does not keep the old calibration valid: Raman adds complementary information and a combined NIR+Raman model is built on newly fused data, so it is a new model that needs its own calibration and validation on the new formulation, and whether fusion helps this blend is a hypothesis.
Raman signals are weak and can be masked by much stronger fluorescence of many organic compounds, so check the new API and excipients for fluorescence at 785 nm before committing to Raman.
NIR spans 780–2500 nm while Vis-NIR silica fiber transmits 350–2400 nm, so confirm that the existing fiber and spectrometer cover the spectral region used by the new model.

methods.why: It is the existing pilot method, suits powders with 0.5–1 mm depth and remote fiber probes, but needs a new chemometric calibration for the new blend.
The same quantity in the same location was measured with fused NIR+Raman PLS, which outperformed single methods in that study, so it is worth testing against NIR alone.
Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups in powders with 2–5 mm depth and high selectivity, but may be masked by fluorescence.
Strong mid-IR absorption limits ATR to very thin layers and it is rated for liquids, pastes and soft solids, not flowing powder in a feed frame.

questions.q: What API concentration range must the new formulation cover, and what accuracy do you need?
questions.why: The new calibration design and the go/no-go criteria depend on the range and target performance.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory method will provide reference API values for samples taken at the feed frame?
questions.why: A new chemometric model must be built and validated against independent reference data.

questions.q: What are the new API and excipients, and are any of them known to fluoresce?
questions.why: Fluorescence can mask the weak Raman signal and decide whether Raman is usable.

questions.q: Which NIR probe, spectrometer range, fiber type and fiber length does the existing pilot use?
questions.why: The fiber must transmit the NIR range used by the model and Raman needs silica fiber without jacket fluorescence.

questions.q: Is there room in the feed frame for a second probe or a combined NIR+Raman probe?
questions.why: Heterogeneous powder needs both methods to see the same spot or at least synchronised data, and a combined probe fitting a feed frame exists.

technical.spectral_window: NIR 780–2500 nm, limited to 350–2400 nm by Vis-NIR silica fiber; Raman excitation 785 nm, Raman shift range unknown – ask.
technical.probe: NIR diffuse reflection probe for powder (0.5–1 mm depth) and Raman contact probe (785 nm, 2–5 mm depth) or combined NIRaman feed-frame probe; window material unknown – ask.
technical.fiber: Vis-NIR silica for NIR, Al/Cu-coated silica for Raman; length and routing unknown – ask; fibers keep spectrometers away from vibration and dust.
technical.process_conditions: Feed frame of a rotary tablet press; temperature, powder speed, cleaning and hazardous-area classification unknown – ask.
technical.sampling: Measurement point in the feed frame; sampling rate and response time unknown – ask; NIR and Raman spectra must be time-synchronised.
technical.reference_method: Independent laboratory API assay of samples taken at the feed frame; method unknown – ask.
technical.calibration: New calibration on the new blend covering the API range (unknown – ask); first re-test the old NIR model on the new blend, then build NIR, Raman and fused PLS models validated on the same independent samples.

experiment.objective: Determine whether a new NIR calibration, Raman, or a fused NIR+Raman model best predicts API concentration of the new blend in the feed frame.
steps: Apply the existing NIR model to the new blend and compare its predictions with independent laboratory reference values to document whether it fails.
Prepare new-blend samples spanning the client's API range and check the new API and excipients for fluorescence under 785 nm Raman excitation.
Record time-synchronised NIR diffuse reflection and 785 nm Raman spectra in the feed frame, ideally with a combined probe sampling the same spot, and take matching samples for the reference assay.
Build NIR-only, Raman-only and low-level fused NIR+Raman PLS models and compare them on the same independent validation set.
references: Independent laboratory API assay of feed-frame samples (method to be specified by the client)
experiment.go_no_go: Acceptance criteria (accuracy, range, response time) to be set by the client; the fused model is adopted only if it beats the best single method on the same validation data.

pathway.key_features: Not yet available; no spectra of the new blend were supplied, so key spectral features must be selected after the multi-method test.
pathway.path_reason: The method and model must first be selected by a multi-method test on the new blend before choosing a tailored solution.

multispectral.why: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and asymmetric polar groups while Raman sees the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups, and this pair was used for blend potency in a feed frame.
multispectral.probe: combined probe (same spot), e.g. a NIRaman probe that fits the feed frame; otherwise separate synchronised probes
multispectral.fusion: low-level fusion of synchronised spectra with dedicated fusion handling, then PLS
multispectral.test: Build NIR-only, Raman-only and fused models on the same new-blend samples and accept the combination only if it beats the best single method on the same independent validation data.

assumptions: The existing NIR pilot uses a diffuse reflection probe in the feed frame.
Samples of the new blend at several API levels can be produced for calibration.
An independent laboratory assay for API content is available.
